extracted.subtask_description: An Associated Press newswire report covering multiple developments related to the Korean War, union disputes, diplomatic negotiations and a military drug test. The text is a historical news dispatch aimed at informing the public about ongoing political, military and social events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 10, Section 8 — eligibility for local union office
rubrics_metrics.description: "No member of any local union shall be eligible to hold an elective position ... if he is a member of or subservient to a political organization, such as the Communist, Fascist or Nazi which owes its allegiance to any government other than ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by the UAW administrative board to remove five local officers; removals made under Article 10, Section 8 and subject to local union trial board and general council votes (example: local general council rejected the board's verdict by 94-21). The clause functions as a procedural standard for disqualifying officers for political affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Armistice supervision — ports of entry and neutral inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Allied proposal that five ports of entry (specific cities named for North and South Korea) be designated through which troop replacements and supplies would move during an armistice and that these ports be open to neutral inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allied staff insisted airfields and seaports in the vicinity of each city should be open for neutral inspection; Communists objected and appeared to want inspections confined within city limits. Selection of ports and whether airfields/seaports are inspectable are treated as key conditions for supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisoner exchange — basis of 'data already exchanged' and 'step-by-step' progress vs. voluntary repatriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Communists proposed that exchange plans could be worked out on the basis of 'data already exchanged' and by 'step-by-step' progress; Allies argued for voluntary repatriation and sought clarification on what the Communists meant by these terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allied negotiators posed seven questions to clarify the Communist position, including whether prisoners would be given any choice as to their side and whether some prisoners held by the U.N. would have to be turned over to the Communists even if forced (e.g., 'use bayonets and shackles'). The procedural interpretation of 'data already exchanged' and 'step-by-step' are decisive for acceptable exchange mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug testing standard — requirement to 'furnish conclusive proof' of PR 9000 efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army announced tests of a new antimalarial drug (PR 9000) 'to furnish conclusive proof' of the drug's ability to prevent malaria; tests involve about 9,000 soldier volunteers (Korean War veterans without recorded malaria history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing sites named (Ft. Dix, Ft. Knox, Camp Breckinridge, Ft. Benning); supervision by named medical researchers; rationale to start tests before summer when malaria recurrence is likeliest. The description includes volunteer selection criteria (returning by surface ship and not previously given primaquine), treatment regimen considerations (primaquine found effective against liver phase; 14-day treatment), and organizational oversight (Army Medical Research and Development Board chair in charge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Truce supervision — limits on external policing and construction of military airfields
rubrics_metrics.description: Major unresolved issues for truce supervision include whether Russia should be allowed to help police an armistice and the question of permitting the building of military airfields during an armistice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Allies flatly rejected both Russian participation in policing an armistice and Communist demands to build/repair military airfields; these points are presented as critical stumbling blocks to finalizing armistice policing arrangements.
